note: The eject up to the lip tip, at 12 V and a 50 mm stand-off: the state it leaves the lip in starts the 3D second-trip trial.

assumes.text: The pipe arrives square to the chute and stays square, its axis across the robot.

The robot's pipe-contact surfaces are the contact lines of the pocket section (inlet, floor, hood, flare and lip), typed from the design's parameters; the drawn solids sit 2.5 mm (lip 3.5 mm) below them as the clearance reserve.
Each roller is its 2 in tread circle on the axis the parameters place, with the tread's compliance as its contact spring; the drawn roller solid is only the rigid core, so the tread is typed.
The section is 20 mm off the pipe's centre plane, where the official station chute plate is solid; at the centre plane it is cut by one of its 32 mm slots, which the 302 mm pipe bridges.

The pipe starts at rest on the design's carry seat, the nominal receive's end state, whatever the tread stiffness; the recorded campaign started each stiffness at its own receive seat (304.10 to 308.57 mm).

inertiaKgM2.note: 1.6 mm polycarbonate plate about its pin: an estimate

preloadNm.note: Torsion spring preload, set on assembly; the recorded campaign tried 0.01 as a weak spring

dampingNmSPerRad.note: Pin friction as viscous damping: an estimate

control.note: The interlock withholds the eject: the nip stays on its hold and the pipe must not leave.
